Interactive synteny plots

Source: vignettes/articles/interactive.Rmd
interactive.Rmd

Every ggsynteny plot can be made interactive with ggiraph: build the plot with interactive = TRUE, then render it with syn_girafe(). Hovering a ribbon fades everything else and shows a tooltip with the block (or link) coordinates; hovering a chromosome or gene shows what it is. The widgets work anywhere HTML does — R Markdown, Quarto, Shiny, pkgdown.

library(ggsynteny)

Macro-synteny: hover the rice-sorghum blocks

Hover a ribbon to isolate one collinear block and read its coordinates; hover a chromosome for its size. Scroll/pinch to zoom (up to 4x).

data(rice_sorghum)

p <- plot_synteny(rice_sorghum, c("Rice", "Sorghum"),
                  palette = "casa_natal",
                  chr_fill = "per_chr", ribbon_fill = "source_chr",
                  interactive = TRUE)
syn_girafe(p, width_svg = 10, height_svg = 5)

Micro-synteny: hover genes and homology links

Gene tooltips show name, contig, coordinates and strand; link tooltips show the connected gene pair and its percent identity:

micro <- demo_microsynteny_data()

p <- plot_microsynteny(micro$features, micro$links,
                       bin_order = c("ZONMW-30", "ZONMW-20", "ZONMW-10"),
                       palette = "casa_natal",
                       interactive = TRUE)
syn_girafe(p, width_svg = 10, height_svg = 4.5)

Styling the widget

syn_girafe() exposes the SVG size, the hover CSS, and takes any extra ggiraph::opts_*() through opts:

syn_girafe(p,
           width_svg = 12, height_svg = 5,
           hover_css = "fill-opacity:1;stroke:#000;stroke-width:1.5px;",
           opts = list(ggiraph::opts_toolbar(position = "topright")))

Everything else about the plot — palettes, fills, curvature — is exactly as in the static version, so interactive = TRUE can be flipped on at the very end of your workflow.
